Normalized signed-state map H(u)=1/[1+kappa(u-1)], z'=d z+(1-d)H(u), u'=u(2min(H(u),z')-1), kappa∈[.45,.55], is an invariant strict contraction on [0.7,1.3]^2. Independently checked rational uniform derivative bounds F∈[18000/54289,22000/29929], |H'|≤22000/27889, row norms at most about 0.95503 and 0.81630, strictly below 24/25; min-switch continuous piecewise smooth. Thus every source trajectory obeys |x_t-(-1)^t r|≤(13/50)r (24/25)^(t-1) and approaches positive nonminimizer objective. For small strictly positive beta1,beta2 a four-state signed map has contracting autonomous fixed point and exponentially decaying bias-correction perturbations; finite-source entry and uniform contraction give persistence. Independently replayed actual printed bias-corrected recurrences 150 steps for (0,0),(.0002,.0001),(.001,.002) and confirmed initial objective decrease and limiting two-cycle; finite traces only corroborate the analytic proof.
